research.job_description_summary: Adobe hires new graduates in India as Member of Technical Staff (MTS-1). Glassdoor reviews describe on-campus interviews with medium-difficulty problems on hash maps, linked lists and trees (September 2026), and a four-round technical process in March 2025 (projects and a sliding-window problem with DBMS, OS and distributed-systems questions; a tree problem with Java and C++ semantics; a managerial round with a monotonic-stack problem, concurrency, web APIs and a lift design; and a director round with KMP and Kadane implementations). The official careers pages were not fetched.
limitations: Adobe's official careers pages were not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

Most B items come from one Glassdoor review (interviewed March 2025). The reviewer's director round asks about 'reasons for changing jobs', which suggests a lateral hire, so some topics may reflect experienced-hire loops and may be harder than typical new-graduate interviews.
A September 2026 on-campus review gives only the topic area (hash maps, linked lists, trees), not problems; the OA-style items are original practice.
A 2022 review (online test, binary search tree focus) is older than the 2025 cutoff and was used only as topic context.
Reported items carry one report each and are unverified.
Behavioral and design prompts beyond the reported lift system are original practice.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.

questions.notes: The topic is reported in candidate accounts or guides; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.fr/Entretien/Adobe-Entretien-E1090-RVW105408080.htm.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between shared and exclusive locks? What is a deadlock in a database and how is it resolved?
questions.relevance_to_role: A March 2025 review describes a one-hour technical round with projects, a sliding-window problem, DBMS, OS and distributed-systems questions.
questions.expected_answer: Shared locks allow concurrent reads; exclusive locks allow one writer. Database deadlocks form from circular lock waits; the DBMS detects them via a wait-for graph and aborts one victim.
follow_ups: What is optimistic locking?
questions.notes: The topic is reported in candidate accounts or guides; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.fr/Entretien/Adobe-Entretien-E1090-RVW105408080.htm.

questions.prompt: How do indexes work, and what is the cost of an index?
questions.relevance_to_role: A March 2025 review describes a one-hour technical round with projects, a sliding-window problem, DBMS, OS and distributed-systems questions.
questions.expected_answer: A B-tree index narrows lookups to O(log n). It increases write cost and storage, and is useful for selective columns and range queries.
follow_ups: What is a composite index and why does column order matter?
questions.notes: The topic is reported in candidate accounts or guides; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.fr/Entretien/Adobe-Entretien-E1090-RVW105408080.htm.

questions.relevance_to_role: A March 2025 review describes a one-hour technical round with projects, a sliding-window problem, DBMS, OS and distributed-systems questions.
questions.expected_answer: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Prevent by lock ordering, timeouts, or acquiring all resources up front.
